- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model spikes sharply after a recent positive sentiment spike, it overreacts; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high or 20% below true outcome if sentiment drops.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.33) and model forecasts remain high, it overestimates; apply downward bias of 15–30% for 3–7 day horizon.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 1.80), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 5–15% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from negative to positive, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 5–10% within 2–3 days of sentiment change.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently forecasts >2.5x recent 18-day average, it is overconfident; cap at 1.8x average or 20% below true outcome.  
- If sentiment is low and true outcome is volatile (e.g., 3+ days of ±0.30 range), model overreacts; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 20–40%.
